b: Every day, someone posts about how broken Meta is...
While it could be, there are parts of meta I never see people discuss or talk about.
On a few occasions, when I see these posts, I've asked for ads account to give them feedback.
The feedback is free, and I don't want clients
The consistent thing I see over and over again and within our own account, is people aren't good at copywriting or positioning.
Two months ago we had 30 companies pop up selling a fake product that looked like ours but wasn't.
Suddenly it appeared that our ads tanked.
The next they were down, burning money.
When we investigated, they'd stolen our ads. Not the angles, like actually ripped our ads, from our founder and were running them.
We Ran A Campaign About Scam Companies
Our cac returned, and then we were on the warpath.
And in a market that became incredibly competitive overnight, where the customers were seeing the same exact message by 30 other companies...
... The customers had no clue where to turn or who to trust.
So Making More Creative Isn't The Fix, If You Don't Understand Market Positioning
With A.i. It's Easier Than Every To Copy A Message & Business
And I see all the not skilled marketers just copying everything they see.
The entire internet is just copying, and copying.
We recently just launched a product in a market, that is actually very saturated.
Because the Ecom space is actually pretty small, we know our competitors CAC.
And we've started a campaign that is actually 1/3 of their CAC.
How are we able to do this?
When you see an ad and click, you then see a bunch from all the competitors...
So in order to cut through, you've got to deposition.
What is actually different, unique or something specific all reviews say that nobody is calling out.
Can you run direct attack ads at your competition and reposition your product in the mind of the audience.
We have several attack ads, that are actually true, and we are now striking hard at the market.
Customers loving our ads, and we also providing a reason why they failed with our competitors products, so they give us a try.
In any market there are really only two companies that can own it.
Pepsi and Coke are pretty much own the cola market. Everyone else fights over the last 10%
You can read the book called 22 imutable laws about positioning from al reiss and his partner, I forget his name.
But the up and down yo yo, that I've found to happen is when our ads don't say anything unique.
Meta doesn't know the difference, the audience doesn't know the difference.
And we see the same exact shit.
If you're selling something you have competition.
And if you're not repositioning your products so the consumer knows why to use your's over the competition, then you're not going to get market penetration.
Which means more creative, that isn't actually different, or unique, won't cut through the market.
And it doesn't matter how much creative you produce, if it's just throwing spaghetti at the wall, then you're definitely not getting market position.
Everyone will just call cap, which is fine, but I'm helping to run some of the bigger brands on the market, and this newer product we're directly competing with P&G in new categories.
If you have any questions, feel free to ask.
I'm not looking for clients, so if you're just going to comment that, I'm not going to respond to your limiting beliefs.
Hope this helps one person out there that things meta is stacked against you. It can feel that way, but the markets are very competitive these days.
